The recorded input element therefore gains `data-disable-with="Subscribe"`; nothing else about the page moves. The default is the framework's, above the template, and restoring the 4.2 markup would mean either setting the flag back to false or passing `data: { disable_with: false }` at the call site -- both of them code written to undo a documented change.

subscriptions/sub.location_after_confirm.why: A location page (`locations/show`), whose subscription form ends in `f.submit 'Subscribe'` (app/views/locations/_email_notifications.html.erb:10, the partial `show.html.erb:8` renders). `FormBuilder#submit` is `submit_tag` with the form's own default label filled in, and Rails 5.0 turned on `ActionView::Base.automatically_disable_submit_tag`, so every `submit_tag` now emits `data-disable-with` carrying its own label unless the call opts out. The recorded input element therefore gains `data-disable-with="Subscribe"`; nothing else about the page moves. The default is the framework's, above the template, and restoring the 4.2 markup would mean either setting the flag back to false or passing `data: { disable_with: false }` at the call site -- both of them code written to undo a documented change.
